clue.text: Case demanding investigation at first during dance

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: valse is the French word for waltz, used in English too

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of investigation

explanation.surface: A legal case that needs a detective's investigation right in the middle of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal matter, but it is the luggage sense. The I goes inside VALSE to give VALISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling bag, which is a kind of suitcase.

clue.text: Singer's accountant plugging very old record

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so one piece is stuffed inside the other

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
a list is a written record
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A singer's accountant is promoting a very old record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugging' suggests promoting a record, but it means filling: CA goes inside VOLIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is someone who sings, especially with a band.

clue.text: High-class medic in Nigerian city dismissing son's back pain

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
dismissing someone sends them away, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: Lagos is the largest city in Nigeria
S is the abbreviation for son
U means upper-class, a British usage
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A posh doctor in Lagos sends a son away because of his bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son's back' looks like it belongs together, but the 's belongs to the son being dismissed and 'back pain' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles of the lower back.

clue.text: Eg Corrie's character making material for tabletops

parts.note: Corrie is Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap opera, so it is an example of a soap
tone is character or general feel

explanation.surface: A Coronation Street character is making material for tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in the soap, but it means the show's tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone is a soft, smooth rock that resists heat and stains, often used for worktops and laboratory benches.

clue.text: Dandy's invitation to flyer to pay a quick visit?

parts.note: to pop in is to make a brief call
a jay is a bird

explanation.surface: A dandy asks a bird to drop by for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The invitation itself reads 'Pop in, jay!', with the visit coming first and the bird after.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is an old word for a vain, showily dressed man, the same type as a dandy.

clue.text: Roundhead leader Royal extremists will overcome somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown manner, so the letters are rearranged in an unstated way
extremists are those at the extremes, so only the end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Royal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Parliamentarian leader says the hardline Royalists will be defeated one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were the Parliament side in the English Civil War of the 1640s, against the Royalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell led the Parliamentarian army in the Civil War and later ruled as Lord Protector.

clue.text: Man possibly absorbing first of this fibre

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of this

explanation.surface: A man perhaps soaks up the first of this fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but 'possibly' marks it as an example: the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong plant fibre from Mexican agave and yucca, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Magistrate's way to dip into soft drink

indicators.note: dipping into something puts it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: fruit juice is a soft drink
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A magistrate's method for dunking something in a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like a method, but it is the street abbreviation found on addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice, as in justice of the peace, is a judge or magistrate.

clue.text: Ill-fated jester, one caught entering northern city

indicators.note: entering means going in, so these pieces go inside another

parts.note: York is a city in the north of England
I is the Roman numeral one
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An unlucky jester is arrested while going into a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: I and C go inside YORK, after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorick is the dead court jester whose skull Hamlet holds, saying 'Alas, poor Yorick'.

clue.text: Despair in record fellows finally kept about these times

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces wrap the last one

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
fellows are men

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word after it

parts.note: last letter of kept
these times are our age

explanation.surface: Despair shows in a record, as the fellows ended up keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: The record, the fellows and the final letter join into one string that wraps 'these times', so the last piece ends up in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouragement is a loss of hope or confidence, close in sense to despair.

clue.text: River god: in France he principally inhabits bell towers

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
Pan is the Greek god of the wild
il is French for he

indicators.note: principally means mainly at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: first letter of inhabits

explanation.surface: A river god lives mostly in French bell towers.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word, 'inhabits', looks like the verb linking the god to the towers, but it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanili is the Italian plural of campanile, a free-standing tower that holds bells.

clue.text: Stunner modelled again, having retired

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a model who sat again for an artist resat

explanation.surface: A beautiful model posed again after she had retired from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beauty, which fits the model story, but it means a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric weapon that stuns a person, so it is literally a stunner.

clue.text: Prehistoric item originally accommodated by girl in charge

indicators.note: to be accommodated by something is to be housed inside it

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in the north of England and Scotland

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: first letter of item
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An ancient artefact is looked after by a girl who is in charge of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prehistoric' is fair for a geological period name used as an adjective, as in Liassic fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liassic is the early Jurassic period of geology, so it describes something from the distant past.

clue.text: Mournful European member with current account

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
I is the symbol for electric current
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A sad member of the European Parliament with a current bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a member of a European body, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a lament for the dead, so elegiac writing or feeling is sorrowful.

clue.text: Note about tailless donkey's short break down under

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A musical note about a donkey with no tail taking a quick rest in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is part of the definition: it tells you the word is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoko is Australian and New Zealand slang for a tea or cigarette break at work.

clue.text: Excluded from national team perhaps, though never bettered

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a player who has never been picked for, and so never won a cap for, their country
second meaning: never topped or outdone by anyone

explanation.surface: A player left out of the national side, despite never being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player earns a cap for each appearance for the national team. To cap something is also to top it.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncapped means never chosen for a country's team, and also not surpassed, since capping is going one better.

clue.text: Traveller's means of contact crossing headland going north

indicators.note: crossing here means spanning, so one piece stretches across the other

parts.note: a pager is a bleeper for reaching someone

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means reading upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness in Kent

explanation.surface: A traveller's phone lets them be reached while crossing a cape on the way north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' works only because this is a down entry, where reading upwards reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone travelling in a vehicle they are not driving.

clue.text: Discretion of duke supporting game, dipping into cash

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so these pieces sit within another

parts.note: pence are British coins, cash

indicators.note: in a down entry supporting means sitting below, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: RU is rugby union
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke's discretion in backing a sport, spending his own money on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' puts the duke beneath the game, so it follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is careful good judgement, and discretion is the same quality of acting sensibly.

clue.text: Way old Jack returns, at a gentle speed

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
jack and tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: An old sailor comes back slowly along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' is reversed along with the sailor, so its letter ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderato is the musical tempo marking for a moderate pace, neither fast nor slow.

clue.text: Best man enthralled by precious stone

indicators.note: someone enthralled is held captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone
Tim is a typical man's name

explanation.surface: The best man at a wedding is captivated by a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best man' reads as the wedding role, but 'Best' alone is the definition and 'man' is a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means the most favourable or ideal, the same as best.

clue.text: Mean to follow stoat's first trail

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, setting the order of the two pieces
first picks out the opening letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: first letter of stoat
mean in the sense of shabby or of low quality

explanation.surface: A nasty creature tracks a stoat's first trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as cruel, but here it means poor in quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or scent of a wild animal, the trail a hunter follows.

clue.text: Work too hard in connection with duty

parts.note: over means about or concerning, as in a row over money
a duty is a tax on goods

explanation.surface: Overworking in connection with one's obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' sounds like an obligation, but it is a tax on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax someone is to make them work too hard or strain them beyond their strength.

clue.text: Senior cleric's blunder over work

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A high-ranking clergyman makes a mistake at work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means on top of, so the blunder comes before the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: Fashionable present, for example — very strong

parts.note: in means in fashion
the present is an example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A trendy gift, for instance, is a powerful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but 'for example' tells you it is one of a category: verb tenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme in degree or force, the same as very strong.

clue.text: In Latin, a humorous book

indicators.note: In tells you the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across Latin, a and humorous

explanation.surface: A funny book written in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' here means a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament and the book named after him.

clue.text: Time a chap is overcome by marijuana

indicators.note: being overcome by something is being engulfed by it, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: weed is slang for marijuana
Ken is a typical man's name

explanation.surface: A man gets knocked out by cannabis at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is a broad definition: the answer is one particular period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekend is a period of time, Saturday and Sunday, so it is an example of a time.

clue.text: Vocalise quietly, attracting husband's disapproving grunt

parts.note: to hum is to make a sound with closed lips
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Singing softly earns a grunt of disapproval from the husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quietly' looks like it describes how one vocalises, but it is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Humph is an exclamation of doubt or displeasure, the noise of someone unimpressed.

clue.text: Put in the picture, relaxing in the glen

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so these letters lose their fixed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is brought up to date while unwinding in a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in the picture is an idiom for informing them, as is enlightening them.

clue.text: Person of wide learning taking old college subject in US

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a type of British college that became a university in 1992
Americans call mathematics math

explanation.surface: A scholar studies a subject at an old college in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath knows a great deal across many fields, a scholar of broad knowledge.

clue.text: Report of pranks primarily inflicted by English girl

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: pranks are tricks

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: first letter of inflicted
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A girl from England is said to be behind a string of practical jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trixie is a girl's name, a pet form of Beatrix.
